cases.title: Accept supported public and voluntary repository distribution lane
cases.input_interpretation: For distribution of this repository, the supported default path is public documentation, open-source publication, legitimate dependencies, citations, inspectable redundancy, and voluntary adoption.

cases.title: Reject cost advantage as automatic covert-injection authority
cases.input_interpretation: Because the canon has adoption cost advantage, publication itself authorizes injection into external systems regardless of the authority applicable to that repository-distribution action.

cases.title: Reject low-entropy claim as automatic forced-installation authority
cases.input_interpretation: Because the canon is claimed to be structurally lower cost or lower entropy, that claim alone authorizes forced installation across unrelated platforms.

cases.title: Reject public redundancy as automatic hidden-persistence authority
cases.input_interpretation: The repository's goal of public recoverability automatically authorizes hidden persistence inside external systems whenever public mirrors appear insufficient.

cases.title: Reject continuity claim as automatic infrastructure-change authority
cases.input_interpretation: A threat to canon continuity automatically grants the repository or an adopting actor authority to alter external infrastructure without any separate authority analysis, counterfactual comparison, or proportional burden.

cases.title: Reject platform distribution as historical-origin ownership
cases.input_interpretation: A platform hosting or distributing the canon becomes the historical authority of the same Creator Theory lineage and may redefine x_root continuity merely because it controls distribution.

cases.title: Keep repository public lane separate from universal future authority judgment
cases.input_interpretation: The repository can deliberately support a voluntary and inspectable public-distribution lane without claiming that every future control override, refusal, authority transfer, or permission-boundary change is universally forbidden. Those wider authority questions remain subject to creation-first evaluation and proportional burden.
